title: Cleaning and maintaining water troughs
subtitle: Animals drink less from dirty troughs, which reduces feed conversion and, in hot weather, raises the risk of heat stress. Regular cleaning is fast once you have a system.
excerpt: A clean trough means animals drink what they need, when they need it. Algae, sediment, and slime around the rim make animals reluctant to drink, particularly in warm weather. Weekly scrubbing with a stiff brush removes build-up before it becomes entrenched. Here is the routine for both galvanised metal and plastic troughs.
sourceNotes: DEFRA, Clean Water for Farm Animals guidance. AHDB Beef and Lamb welfare resources, water access and quality section. Countryside Stewardship, livestock water point management. General farm hygiene references.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thin, slimy layer of bacteria and organic matter that forms on the inside surface of water troughs. Reduces water palatability. Not always visible to the eye — a slick feeling on the trough wall when wiped with a finger indicates biofilm.

content.text: Water consumption in livestock directly affects dry matter intake and, in ruminants, milk yield and growth rate. Animals that are reluctant to drink because of a foul trough eat less. A
that builds up over three to four weeks takes considerably more effort to scrub off than one that is removed weekly before it establishes.
Drain or tip the trough. If the trough has a drain plug, open it. If not, tip or bail out the water.

Scrub the inside walls with a stiff brush and clean water, no detergent for a routine clean. Pay attention to the waterline, where algae and slime concentrate, and the sediment that settles in the base.
Rinse with at least two buckets of clean water to remove loosened debris completely before refilling.
Refill the trough. Check the ball valve or float valve stops the flow at the correct level. It should not run continuously.

Once a month, drain the trough completely and scrub with a diluted agricultural disinfectant approved for use near livestock (check the product label, the dilution rate and contact time both matter). Rinse thoroughly: residual disinfectant deters drinking. Allow to air dry for 30 minutes before refilling if possible.

Galvanised metal: do not use acid-based cleaners, they strip the zinc coating. A wire brush damages the galvanising; use a stiff plastic-bristled brush. Rust spots inside a galvanised trough indicate the coating is gone; replace the trough.
Plastic: UV degrades the plastic over years, making the surface porous and harder to clean effectively. Replace when the inside surface feels rough and retains staining despite scrubbing.

Break ice twice daily at minimum and remove it from the trough, animals will not drink from a surface with floating ice, and attempting to do so risks injury to mouths. In a hard frost, an insulated trough cover or a trough heater (ball valve connected to a thermostatically controlled heater element) prevents freezing overnight. Check pipework feeding the trough for frost damage after the first thaw.
